content: The Journal of Experimental Medicine (JEM) is a peer-reviewed academic journal that focuses on publishing research articles and commentaries in the field of biomedical science. The topics it addresses include immunology, inflammation, infectious diseases, hematopoiesis, cancer, stem cell biology, and vascular biology. Historically, the journal has primarily published basic research studies, but there has been a growing inclusion of studies involving human subjects, which accounted for approximately 10% of the published papers in 2004. JEM was established in 1896, making it one of the oldest scientific journals in existence. Initially, it was published by Johns Hopkins University, but in 1905, the Rockefeller University Press assumed responsibility for its publication. The journal operates on a not-for-profit basis. Unlike many journals, JEM does not have a single Editor-in-Chief; instead, it is managed by a team of eleven academic editors and supported by an advisory board consisting of approximately one hundred members. The journal is published on a monthly basis. It maintains an extensive online archive of articles dating back to its inception in 1896. Articles are available in both text and PDF formats, although material published in 1996 and earlier is accessible only in PDF format. Articles that are older than six months are freely available to the public, and the journal also provides free access to all its content for readers in developing countries. In 2005, JEM had an impact factor of 13.965, placing it among the most influential journals in the biomedical sciences.
